positions.claim: Writing specification and design documents before code produces higher-quality output from coding assistants, not just faster output.
Coding assistants left unguided will go off the rails, so explicit up-front documents are needed as guardrails.
Better frontier models and built-in planning/thinking modes do not eliminate the need for human-reviewed spec documents.
Putting too much information into agents.md or steering files is harmful; there is a Goldilocks amount of context.
The human, not the agent, is accountable for generated code and must personally review both the code and the spec documents.
More people are now using CLI coding assistants than IDE-based ones.
Spec-driven development is a workflow, not a product feature — it can be done manually with any assistant or with GitHub's open-source Spec Kit.
Spec-driven development applies to existing legacy codebases, not only greenfield projects.
Small changes and quick fixes may not justify the spec workflow and are better handled by vibe coding.
Generated design and requirements documents should always be hand-edited by the developer before implementation, since output quality is bounded by input quality.
Property-based tests derived from the requirements and design documents are worth generating and running to verify tasks were implemented correctly.
MCP is not dead; it is still maturing and remains valuable, particularly for pulling ticket and requirements data from tools like Jira or Asana into the spec flow.
Requirements and design can be authored in either order — starting from the design document first is a legitimate variant of the flow.
